title: HMS - Harmful Brain Activity Classification
prompt: Classify patterns of harmful brain activity in EEG recordings to assist doctors in detecting seizures and other critical states. Data: 50-second EEG segments (sampled at 200Hz) and corresponding spectrograms. Goal: Predict the probability distribution across six classes of brain activity (Seizure, LPD, GPD, LRDA, GRDA, Other). Challenge: High noise in raw EEG and inter-rater variability in human labels.
solution_summary: Ensemble of 1D and 2D CNN models. 1st place team (Sony) transformed raw EEG into 2D scalogram images using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and bipolar montages. They used a 2-stage training process: first training on the full noisy dataset and then fine-tuning on high-quality labels (10+ human votes). Key insight was using 'entmax' with a small alpha (1.03) to sharpen class probabilities.

title: NeurIPS 2024 - Predict New Medicines with BELKA
prompt: Predict the binding affinity of small molecules to specific protein targets to accelerate drug discovery. Data: 133M chemical compounds represented as SMILES strings, with binding results from a DNA-encoded chemical library (DEL). Goal: Classify each molecule as a binder or non-binder for three proteins. Challenge: Extreme class imbalance and the need to generalize to 'unseen' chemical building blocks.
solution_summary: A minimalist Transformer-based approach. The winning solution used a simple 4-layer Transformer encoder with 8 heads, treating SMILES as a character-level text problem. The critical success factor was a two-stage pre-training: first using Masked Language Modeling (MLM) and second predicting ECFP fingerprints (SMILES-to-ECFP) before fine-tuning on the competition data. This allowed the model to learn robust chemical representations.

title: UBC-OCEAN: Ovarian Cancer Subtype Classification and Outlier Detection
prompt: Classify ovarian cancer subtypes from high-resolution histopathology images and identify rare variants. Data: Whole-slide images (WSI) and tissue microarrays (TMA). Goal: Predict one of five subtypes (CC, EC, HGSC, LGSC, MC) or 'Other'. Challenge: WSIs are multi-gigabyte files with varied magnifications, and models must handle outliers not seen in the training set.
solution_summary: Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) pipeline using foundation model embeddings. The 1st place solution (Owkin) extracted features from image tiles using Phikon (a digital pathology foundation model). These embeddings were then fed into a 'Chowder' MIL model, which uses top/bottom instances for scoring. Outlier detection for the 'Other' class was handled using high-entropy prediction thresholds.
key_techniques: Balanced training strategy for rare subtypes

title: Optiver - Trading at the Close
prompt: Predict the closing price movements of hundreds of Nasdaq-listed stocks during the final ten minutes of the trading day. Data: Order book imbalance data (sizes and prices), reference prices, and target labels (WAP shifts). Goal: Predict the target value for the next 60 seconds. Challenge: Strict inference time constraints and the need to prevent data leakage in streaming validation.
solution_summary: Ensemble of LightGBM and CatBoost models with a custom online refitting strategy. The 1st place solution focused on 'lead-lag' features and rolling window statistics. They implemented a streaming CV setup to mimic the actual time-series inference. A key post-processing step was 'zero-sum' normalization, ensuring that the net predicted movement across all stocks was zero, reflecting the market-neutral nature of the target.
key_techniques: Revealed target lag features (1, 2, 3 day lags)

title: ISIC 2024 - Skin Cancer Detection with 3D-TBP
prompt: Identify skin cancer (malignant lesions) from low-resolution crops of 3D Total Body Photographs. Data: 400,000+ image crops (typically <256px) and detailed patient/lesion metadata. Goal: Predict the probability of malignancy. Challenge: Extreme class imbalance (0.1% positive rate) and low image quality compared to traditional dermoscopy.
solution_summary: Multimodal fusion of image and tabular features. The top solutions combined 2D CNN backbones (EfficientNetV2, ConvNeXt) for image feature extraction with Gradient Boosting Machines (XGBoost/LightGBM) for patient-level metadata. Models were pre-trained on high-resolution data from previous ISIC years (2018-2020) and fine-tuned on the 2024 low-res images using heavy data augmentation.
key_techniques: Partial AUC optimization via loss weighting

title: LLM - Detect AI Generated Text
prompt: Build a model to detect whether an essay was written by a student or generated by a Large Language Model. Data: Student-written essays from various prompts and AI essays from models like GPT-4 and Llama. Goal: Predict the probability of being AI-generated. Challenge: The test set uses prompts and AI models not seen in the training data, requiring robust generalization.
solution_summary: A hybrid approach combining traditional NLP with Deep Learning. The 1st place solution (Team 'The 1st') relied on an ensemble of TF-IDF / N-gram models and DeBERTa-v3-Large fine-tuned on a massive external dataset of 800k student/AI samples. They used a specific character-level filtering strategy to remove 'prompt-specific' artifacts that caused over-fitting in baseline models.
key_techniques: LGBM/XGBoost on top of TF-IDF scores
Data augmentation with external LLM datasets
Freezing early transformer layers for stability

title: RSNA 2023 Abdominal Trauma Detection
prompt: Detect and grade injuries to internal organs (liver, spleen, kidney, bowel) from abdominal CT scans. Data: 3D CT volumes and organ-level annotations. Goal: Predict injury status and severity for each organ. Challenge: Handling 3D context in multi-slice CT images and the rare occurrence of high-grade injuries.
solution_summary: A multi-stage pipeline utilizing 2.5D and 3D CNNs. 1st place used a 2D model (EfficientNet-B0) to segment/locate organs and extract relevant slices. These slices were then aggregated using a 3D-ConvNeXt or Transformer encoder to capture volumetric context. Final classification was performed using a weighted loss function to prioritize high-grade injuries as per the metric.

title: SenNet + HOA - Hacking the Human Vasculature
prompt: Segment 3D blood vessels from high-resolution Hierarchical Phase-Contrast Tomography (HiP-CT) scans of human kidneys. Data: 3D volumetric images at micron-level resolution. Goal: Predict a binary mask for every voxel. Challenge: Immense data size (terabytes) and the complex, thin topology of microvascular structures.
solution_summary: Ensemble of 2.5D and 3D UNet architectures. The 1st place solution utilized a 3D SegResNet and a 2.5D ConvNeXt-UNet, training on small overlapping crops (patches). They applied heavy morphological post-processing to connect broken vessel segments. A key insight was using pseudo-labeling on unlabeled kidney regions to increase training data diversity.

title: NeurIPS - Ariel Data Challenge 2024
prompt: Extract the atmospheric spectra of exoplanets from raw simulated space telescope observations. Data: Multi-wavelength time-series images (spectral focal plane) covering a transit. Goal: Predict the mean transit depth and uncertainty for 283 wavelengths. Challenge: High jitter noise from the spacecraft and extremely low signal-to-noise ratio.
solution_summary: Physics-informed regression using least-squares optimization. The winning approach involved modeling the transit signal as a product of a polynomial (for baseline/noise) and a step function (for transit depth). They used the Dogbox algorithm (scipy.optimize) for robust fitting. A critical technique was modeling 'jitter spikes' with Lorentzian functions to denoise the pixel-level data before aggregation.
key_techniques: Moving average smoothing with Taylor windows
Weighted Least Squares for depth estimation

title: LEAP - Atmospheric Physics using AI (ClimSim)
prompt: Simulate the sub-grid atmospheric physics (clouds, precipitation, radiation) for climate models. Data: Global dataset of 80 million atmospheric states with input variables like temperature/humidity and output tendencies. Goal: Predict the vertical tendency profiles. Challenge: Massive dataset (700GB+) and the need for high numerical precision in conservation laws.
solution_summary: Deep learning architecture using Transformers and Fourier Neural Operators (FNO). The 1st place solution (Greysnow) employed a vanilla Transformer encoder to process vertical features, coupled with an FNO1D decoder head to predict per-token targets. They used bf16 training to handle the wide dynamic range of features and hdf5 for fast random-access data reading during training.
key_techniques: Bf16 / FP32 mixed training for precision

title: Learning Agency Lab - Automated Essay Scoring 2.0
prompt: Develop an automated system to score student-written essays based on their quality. Data: 17k+ essays written by students (Grades 6-12) with labels from 1 to 6. Goal: Predict the integer score for each essay. Challenge: Achieving human-level grading consistency across different prompts and ensuring model efficiency for real-world classroom use.
solution_summary: Ensemble of fine-tuned Transformer models and feature-based regressors. The 1st place approach combined DeBERTa-v3-Large fine-tuned with a custom QWK loss function and LightGBM models trained on 1,500+ linguistically motivated features (e.g., lexical diversity, grammar errors). They used a 'pseudo-ranking' strategy where the model predicted continuous values before thresholding into integers.

title: Linking Writing Processes to Writing Quality
prompt: Predict essay quality scores from raw keystroke data logged during the writing process. Data: Event-level logs including keys pressed, mouse clicks, and cursor positions over time. Goal: Predict the final score (0.5 - 6.0). Challenge: Extracting high-level writing behaviors (pauses, revisions, burstiness) from extremely granular and long event sequences.
solution_summary: Feature engineering-centric approach using Gradient Boosting. The winning solution (Tomoo) developed over 1,000 features characterizing writing 'bursts' (Productive periods), 'R-bursts' (Revision periods), and 'P-bursts' (Pauses). They used an ensemble of LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost. A key insight was modeling the 'unwritten' time (time spent thinking) as a separate predictive feature.

title: RSNA 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification
prompt: Classify five degenerative lumbar spine conditions from multi-sequence MRI scans. Data: T1, T2, and T2-STIR MRI volumes for each patient. Goal: Predict the severity (Normal/Mild, Moderate, Severe) for each lumbar level (L1-S1). Challenge: Coordinating classification across multiple views (Sagittal/Axial) and localizing the correct spine level.
solution_summary: A 2-stage pipeline consisting of localization and classification. 1st place used a 3D ConvNeXt model to predict 'instance numbers' (slice indices) and coordinates for each vertebrae level. In the second stage, cropped ROI patches from different MRI sequences were fed into a multi-head CNN (ConvNeXt-S/EfficientNet-V2) with a MIL-LSTM head to aggregate features across slices for a final patient-level prediction.

title: Predict Student Performance from Game Play
prompt: Predict whether a student will correctly answer questions in an educational game based on their in-game interaction logs. Data: Clickstream data (room, level, elapsed time) from thousands of game sessions. Goal: Predict correct/incorrect for 18 specific questions. Challenge: Time-series nature of the logs where future performance must be predicted from past interactions.
solution_summary: Session-level feature engineering with Gradient Boosting. The 1st place solution created sophisticated aggregate features over 'levels' and 'rooms' within the game, such as 'time spent per page' and 'click frequency'. They used a separate LightGBM model for each of the 18 questions. A key insight was using 'group-by' features on the sequence of events to capture student frustration or engagement levels.
key_techniques: Level-wise click count and duration stats

title: ICR - Identifying Age-Related Conditions
prompt: Predict whether a person has one of three age-related medical conditions using anonymous health data. Data: 50+ health markers (categorical and numerical) for ~600 patients. Goal: Binary classification of condition presence. Challenge: Extremely small dataset size and highly imbalanced labels, requiring models with very high stability.
solution_summary: Ensemble of diverse tabular models including TabPFN and Gradient Boosting. 1st place used TabPFN (a Prior-Data Fitted Network) which excels on small datasets, alongside XGBoost and LightGBM. They implemented a custom 'stable' cross-validation strategy and used pseudo-labeling to slightly expand the training set. A major component was handling 'epsilon' features through robust imputation.

title: GoDaddy - Microbusiness Density Forecasting
prompt: Forecast the monthly microbusiness density in U.S. counties. Data: Historic density rates, census data, and economic indicators. Goal: Predict density for the next several months. Challenge: The target is highly stable for most counties but volatile in others, making simple models hard to beat.
solution_summary: A 'last-value-plus' strategy with selective ML overrides. The winning approach relied on a weighted combination of 'Last Observed Value' and Linear Regression with trend capping for most counties. They only used CatBoost for counties with high volatility or clear trend shifts identified via outlier detection. Census data (ACS) was used as a static feature for cross-sectional modeling.

title: Stable Diffusion - Image to Prompts
prompt: Reverse-engineer the text prompt used to generate a specific image with Stable Diffusion. Data: Thousands of AI-generated images and their corresponding prompts. Goal: Predict a 384-dimensional embedding representing the prompt. Challenge: Aligning visual style and semantic content in a high-dimensional embedding space.
solution_summary: Fine-tuning Large Vision-Language Models for embedding regression. The 1st place solution fine-tuned CLIP-based backbones (ViT-L-14 and ViT-H-14) using a custom head that mapped visual features directly to the target prompt embedding space. They optimized for Cosine Similarity loss and used a massive auxiliary dataset (LAION-5B) to improve the model's understanding of diverse prompt styles.

title: Feedback Prize - English Language Learning
evaluation_metric: Mean Columnwise Root Mean Squared Error (MCRMSE)
prompt: Evaluate the writing quality of English Language Learners (ELLs) across six categories. Data: Essays written by students for whom English is a second language. Goal: Predict scores (1.0 - 5.0) for Cohesion, Syntax, Vocabulary, Phraseology, Grammar, and Conventions. Challenge: Correlated multi-task targets and varied writing styles.
solution_summary: Multi-task learning with Large Language Models. 1st place used an ensemble of DeBERTa-v3-Large models with a shared backbone and six task-specific regression heads. They applied Multi-Sample Dropout to prevent over-fitting and utilized 'Mean-Pooling' of hidden states from the last 4 layers. A key technique was 'Pseudo-Labeling' using the competition's unlabeled dataset to stabilize the scores.

title: U.S. Patent Phrase to Phrase Matching
prompt: Measure the semantic similarity between two phrases within the context of a patent application. Data: Pairs of 'anchor' and 'target' phrases, along with a 'context' code (CPC category). Goal: Predict similarity on a scale of 0 to 1. Challenge: Understanding technical jargon and the specific nuance of 'context' which changes the meaning of common words.
solution_summary: Context-aware Transformer models. The winning solution concatenated anchor, target, and context description into a single sequence: '[CLS] anchor [SEP] target [SEP] context_description'. They used DeBERTa-v3-Large and ELECTRA-Large backbones. They applied 'Attention Pooling' over the target phrase tokens specifically to highlight the relevant semantic features.

title: NBME - Score Clinical Patient Notes
prompt: Identify specific clinical concepts within patient notes written by medical students. Data: Patient notes and a list of 'features' (e.g., 'chest pain') to find in the text. Goal: Predict the character offsets of the relevant text spans. Challenge: The same concept can be described using many synonyms or abbreviations, and spans can be non-contiguous.
solution_summary: Token classification (NER) with multi-head attention. 1st place treated this as a Question-Answering/NER task using DeBERTa-v3-Large. They formatted the input as 'feature [SEP] patient_note'. The model predicted 'B-I-O' labels for each token. Non-contiguous spans were handled by post-processing overlapping predictions and merging spans that were within a 3-character distance.

title: Mayo Clinic - STRIP AI
prompt: Classify the origin of blood clots (stroke etiology) from high-resolution whole-slide images. Data: Digital pathology slides of blood clots. Goal: Predict if the clot originated from the heart (CE) or the large arteries (LAA). Challenge: WSIs are massive; images often contain a lot of empty space or artifacts, and the CE/LAA distinction is visually subtle.
solution_summary: Tile-based Multiple Instance Learning (MIL). The winning solution used a 'receptive field' approach, extracting thousands of 512x512 tiles from tissue areas. These tiles were encoded by an EfficientNet-B0/B1. The embeddings were then aggregated using a gated-attention MIL head. They also used 'hard negative mining' to focus the model on tissue regions that were most difficult to classify.
key_techniques: Heavy color jitter and stain normalization

title: UW-Madison GI Tract Image Segmentation
prompt: Segment the stomach and intestines in MRI scans to help guide radiation therapy for cancer. Data: 2D MRI slices of the abdomen over multiple days. Goal: Predict masks for Stomach, Large Bowel, and Small Bowel. Challenge: Low contrast between organs and the need for high-precision boundaries to avoid damaging healthy tissue.
solution_summary: 2.5D UNet ensemble with heavy spatial context. 1st place used an ensemble of UNet++ and SegFormer architectures. They used '2.5D' input by stacking 3 consecutive slices (t-1, t, t+1) into RGB channels to provide depth context. They optimized a joint Dice-BCE loss and used test-time augmentation (TTA) with horizontal flipping and scaling.

title: HuBMAP + HPA - Hacking the Human Body
prompt: Segment functional tissue units (FTUs) across different human organs (kidney, lung, prostate, etc.). Data: Histopathology images from different sources with varied staining and resolution. Goal: Predict a binary mask for FTUs in each organ. Challenge: Generalizing across diverse organ types and data sources with differing visual appearances.
solution_summary: An ensemble of high-resolution UNets. The 1st place solution utilized UNet backbones with EfficientNet-B7 and ConvNeXt-Large encoders. They used a large crop size (1024x1024) to capture sufficient FTU context. A crucial step was Organ-specific fine-tuning: training a general model first, then refining it for each organ class using organ-specific data augmentations.

title: Feedback Prize - Predicting Effective Arguments
prompt: Classify the effectiveness of argumentative elements in student essays. Data: Essay snippets labeled as 'Claim', 'Evidence', etc. Goal: Predict if the element is 'Effective', 'Adequate', or 'Ineffective'. Challenge: Contextual dependency; the effectiveness of a 'Claim' depends on the surrounding 'Evidence' and the overall essay flow.
solution_summary: Full-essay context modeling with Transformers. 1st place used DeBERTa-v3-Large where the entire essay was input, and specific markers ([START], [END]) were added around the target discourse element. They used an ensemble of models trained with different seeds and 'Multi-Sample Dropout'. They also used a second-stage LGBM model to aggregate predictions and essay-level features.

title: Coleridge Initiative - Show US the Data
prompt: Identify the names of datasets mentioned in scientific publications. Data: Full-text JSON files of research papers. Goal: Predict the exact string of any dataset mentioned. Challenge: Datasets are often referred to by acronyms, informal names, or aliases not present in any official list.
solution_summary: Hybrid NER and String Matching approach. 1st place combined a transformer-based NER model (SciBERT) to find potential dataset candidates with a 'literal string matching' algorithm against a large dictionary of known datasets. They used a rule-based post-processor to clean acronyms and resolve variations like 'ADNI' vs 'Alzheimer\'s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative'.

title: Google Brain - Ventilator Pressure Prediction
prompt: Predict the pressure inside a mechanical ventilator's circuit based on control signals. Data: Time-series of 'u_in' (air valve) and 'u_out' (exhaust valve) over 80 timesteps. Goal: Predict the pressure at each timestep. Challenge: Capturing the physical dynamics of the lung and mechanical system purely from time-series logs.
solution_summary: Deep sequence modeling with bidirectional LSTMs and GRUs. 1st place used an ensemble of deep (4-8 layers) Bi-LSTMs. They heavily engineered 'delta' features (change in u_in over time) and 'integral' features (cumulative u_in). A key insight was modeling the 'breath' as a single sequence and using a 'Huber Loss' which is more robust to outliers than MSE.

title: G2Net Gravitational Wave Detection
prompt: Detect gravitational wave signals from merging black holes hidden in detector noise. Data: 1D time-series strain data from three detectors (LIGO Hanford, LIGO Livingston, Virgo). Goal: Binary classification (signal present vs. noise). Challenge: Extremely low signal-to-noise ratio where signals are buried in 'colored' Gaussian noise.
solution_summary: Spectrogram-based Computer Vision. 1st place converted the 1D strain data into 2D spectrograms using Constant-Q Transform (CQT). They used an ensemble of EfficientNet-B7 and NFNet-F0 models. They applied 'Whiten' and 'Bandpass' filters to the raw signal before conversion to remove dominant noise frequencies. Data augmentation included frequency and time masking.

title: VinBigData Chest X-ray Abnormalities Detection
prompt: Detect and localize 14 types of thoracic abnormalities in chest X-ray images. Data: Standard DICOM chest X-rays with bounding box annotations from multiple radiologists. Goal: Predict bounding boxes and labels. Challenge: High disagreement between radiologists and the need to filter out false positives from 'noisy' consensus.
solution_summary: Ensemble of Object Detectors with box fusion. 1st place used an ensemble of YOLOv5 and Faster R-CNN (Detectron2). They utilized 'Weighted Boxes Fusion' (WBF) to consolidate overlapping predictions from different models. A key insight was using a separate 'Classifier' model to filter out images with no abnormalities, significantly reducing false positive boxes.

title: Riiid AIEd Challenge 2020
prompt: Predict whether a student will answer a standardized test question correctly based on their learning history. Data: 100M+ interactions (question_id, timestamp, response). Goal: Predict correctness of the next interaction. Challenge: Long-term dependency in student performance and the massive scale of the interaction log.
solution_summary: Transformer-based sequence modeling (SAINT+). 1st place used an encoder-decoder Transformer architecture that separately processed question features (ID, tags) and response features (correctness, elapsed time). They combined this with a LightGBM model that used handcrafted features like 'user-level rolling accuracy' and 'content difficulty' for final blending.
key_techniques: Temporal embedding for 'time since last action'

title: ASHRAE - Great Energy Predictor III
prompt: Predict the energy consumption of buildings across four meter types (electricity, chilled water, steam, hot water). Data: Three years of hourly meter readings, weather data, and building metadata. Goal: Forecast future energy usage. Challenge: Dealing with massive amounts of 'zero' readings, outliers, and data leaks from public sources.
solution_summary: LightGBM ensemble with extensive cleaning. 1st place identified that 'site 0' (UCF) had meter readings in different units (kWh vs kBTU) and corrected them. They used a cross-validation strategy that accounted for the specific time-series structure of each site. They built separate models for each meter type and used weather data imputation to fill missing temperature gaps.

title: Recursion Cellular Image Classification
prompt: Identify biological perturbations (siRNA) in cellular images to help drug discovery. Data: 6-channel microscopy images of cells under 1,108 different siRNA treatments. Goal: Predict which siRNA was applied. Challenge: Significant 'batch effects' between different experimental plates and imaging sites that shift the data distribution.
solution_summary: ArcFace with batch-normalization correction. 1st place used an ensemble of DenseNet and EfficientNet models. To combat batch effects, they implemented a 'Adaptive Batch Norm' where BN statistics were recalculated on a per-plate basis during inference. They also used ArcFace loss to create a discriminative embedding space where siRNA classes were well-separated.

title: Elo Merchant Category Recommendation
prompt: Predict loyalty scores for cardholders based on their transaction history. Data: Card-level metadata and millions of transaction records (historical and new). Goal: Predict the 'loyalty' numerical target. Challenge: Extremely noisy target variable and identifying 'outlier' cardholders who contribute significantly to the total error.
solution_summary: Feature engineering-heavy LightGBM ensemble. 1st place focused on aggregating transaction data at different time grains (monthly, weekly). They used a 'Binary Classifier' as a first stage to detect potential outliers (the -33.219 target value) and a separate regressor for non-outliers. Key features included 'time since last purchase' and 'category concentration' ratios.

title: Humpback Whale Identification
prompt: Identify individual humpback whales from photos of their tails (flukes). Data: 25k images across 5,000+ unique whale IDs. Goal: Predict the whale ID for new images. Challenge: Many whales only have a single photo in the dataset (Few-shot learning), and fluke patterns change slightly over time.
solution_summary: Metric Learning with Siamese Networks. 1st place used an ensemble of ResNet-101 and Senet-154 models. They utilized a 'Triplet Loss' architecture to learn an embedding space where images of the same whale were close together. They also built a separate 'New Whale' classifier to handle the high probability of a whale being previously unseen.

title: Quora Insincere Questions Classification
prompt: Detect insincere or toxic questions on Quora. Data: Text of questions. Goal: Binary classification (sincere vs. insincere). Challenge: Short text lengths and the need for high efficiency, as inference must run in under two hours on a single GPU without internet.
solution_summary: Ensemble of Bi-GRU/LSTM with pre-trained embeddings. 1st place used an ensemble of RNN architectures (Bidirectional GRU and LSTM) with Attention layers. They combined multiple pre-trained word embeddings (GloVe and Paragram) by averaging them. They used 'BucketIterator' for efficient padding and inference within the competition's strict time limits.

title: Google AI Open Images - Visual Relationship Detection
prompt: Identify specific relationships between objects in an image (e.g., 'woman riding horse'). Data: Images with bounding box pairs and relationship labels. Goal: Predict (Subject, Object, Relationship) triplets. Challenge: Combinatorial explosion of possible relationships and identifying subtle interactions.
solution_summary: Relation Proposal Network (RelPN). 1st place used a Faster R-CNN with an FPN backbone to detect subjects and objects. They then used a 'Triplet Head' that took the concatenated features of the subject, object, and their union box to predict the relationship. They utilized a 'Frequency Prior' to boost common relationships found in the training set.
key_techniques: Faster R-CNN with Feature Pyramid Network (FPN)

title: Google Landmark Recognition 2020
prompt: Recognize world landmarks in images across 80,000+ classes. Data: 1.5M images of global landmarks. Goal: Predict the landmark ID and a confidence score. Challenge: Massive number of classes (many with only 1-2 examples) and high visual similarity between different landmarks.
solution_summary: Sub-center ArcFace with Global Descriptors. 1st place used an ensemble of EfficientNet (B7) and ResNet backbones. They used Generalized Mean Pooling (GeM) to extract global descriptors and a 'Sub-center ArcFace' loss, which allows each class to have multiple cluster centers to account for different viewing angles of a landmark.

title: Generative Dog Images
prompt: Generate realistic images of dogs. Data: 20,000 images of various dog breeds. Goal: Submit a generative model (GAN) to produce 10,000 synthetic 64x64 images. Challenge: High image quality and diversity required with limited training data and strict GPU time constraints.
solution_summary: Customized BigGAN architecture. The winning solution utilized a BigGAN-inspired model with 'Spectral Normalization' in both the generator and discriminator. They applied 'Self-Attention' modules to capture global dog structures and used 'Data Augmentation' (flipping, rotation) within the GAN training loop to prevent the discriminator from over-fitting to the small dataset.

title: Northeastern SMILE Lab - Recognizing Faces in the Wild
prompt: Determine if two people are blood relatives based on facial images. Data: Pairs of facial images from the same or different families. Goal: Binary classification (related vs. unrelated). Challenge: Facial features for kinship are subtle and can be obscured by age, lighting, or pose.
solution_summary: Kinship-specific Metric Learning. 1st place used a Siamese network with a ResNet-50 backbone pre-trained on the VGGFace2 dataset. They used a 'Contrastive Loss' to minimize the distance between related pairs and maximize it for unrelated pairs. A key technique was 'Image Triangulation' where they compared children to both parents simultaneously to find shared features.

title: Airbus Ship Detection Challenge
evaluation_metric: F2 Score at different IoU thresholds
prompt: Locate and segment all ships in satellite imagery. Data: High-resolution satellite images with Run-Length Encoded (RLE) masks. Goal: Predict a binary mask for each ship. Challenge: Tiny ships in huge images (768x768), significant class imbalance (mostly empty sea), and close-proximity ships.
solution_summary: 2-stage Detection and Segmentation. 1st place used a 'U-Net' architecture with a ResNet-34 backbone for segmentation. They preceded this with a 'Ship Classifier' (Binary) to remove empty images from the training/inference pipeline. To handle overlapping ships, they used a 'Border Loss' that penalized the model for merging masks of adjacent ships.

title: PUBG Finish Placement Prediction
prompt: Predict the final placement percentile of players in a PUBG match based on their in-game stats. Data: Player stats like kills, distance traveled, and damage dealt. Goal: Predict winPlacePerc (0 to 1). Challenge: The data is grouped by 'match' and 'group' (squad), and the target is relative within each match.
solution_summary: Group-aware MLP and LightGBM. 1st place solution heavily relied on 'group-aggregated' features (mean/max kills in a squad, rank within a match). They used a Deep Neural Network (MLP) with categorical embeddings for match types. They applied a post-processing step to 'rescale' predictions so they followed the discrete ranking structure of the match.

title: TalkingData AdTracking Fraud Detection Challenge
prompt: Detect fraudulent ad clicks in mobile app campaigns. Data: 200M+ click records (IP, app, device, OS, channel, time). Goal: Predict the probability of a click resulting in a download. Challenge: Massive scale of data and the need to capture complex temporal patterns in IP clicking behavior.
solution_summary: Extensive Feature Engineering with LightGBM. 1st place focused on 'Next Click' and 'Previous Click' time-delta features for various feature combinations (e.g., same IP + same App). They used 'Target Encoding' for high-cardinality categories and trained on the full 200M rows using a specific sampling strategy to handle the class imbalance.

title: Google Analytics Customer Revenue Prediction
prompt: Predict the total revenue per customer for the Google Merchandise Store. Data: User-level session logs including geography, device, and traffic source. Goal: Predict the log of (1 + total revenue) for a specific future period. Challenge: Only 1% of users actually make a purchase, leading to a highly zero-inflated target.
solution_summary: 2-stage model with temporal aggregation. 1st place used a classification model to predict 'probability of purchase' followed by a regression model to predict the amount. They aggregated session data into user-level features (e.g., 'total sessions', 'first visit date'). A key insight was modeling the 'time gap' between the training and test periods as a feature.
key_techniques: Handling JSON flattening for nested data

title: Google AI Open Images - Object Detection
prompt: Detect and localize 500 object classes in real-world images. Data: 1.7M images with 12M bounding box annotations. Goal: Predict bounding boxes and labels. Challenge: Massive label hierarchy (e.g., 'Dog' is a parent of 'German Shepherd') and extreme variation in object scales.
solution_summary: Large-scale Object Detection with Cascade R-CNN. 1st place used an ensemble of 'Cascade R-CNN' with 'SENet154' and 'ResNext101' backbones. They used 'Feature Pyramid Networks' (FPN) and 'Soft-NMS' to handle overlapping boxes. They specifically addressed the hierarchy by mapping specific labels to parent categories during training to boost signal for rare classes.

title: Inclusive Images Challenge
prompt: Ensure image classifiers work fairly across different geographic regions. Data: Training data from Western countries, but test data from globally diverse regions (e.g., India, Ethiopia). Goal: Multi-label classification. Challenge: Managing 'geographic bias' where models fail on culturally specific visual representations of the same label.
solution_summary: Robust fine-tuning and domain adaptation. 1st place used an ensemble of ResNet-50 and Inception-v3 models. They utilized 'Pseudo-labeling' on the unlabeled global test set to align the model's feature distribution with the target domains. They also applied heavy 'color augmentation' to reduce the model's reliance on skin tone or lighting conditions typical of Western datasets.
key_techniques: Heavy color jitter and grayscale augmentation

title: Quick, Draw! Doodle Recognition Challenge
prompt: Recognize hand-drawn doodles across 340 categories. Data: Stroke-based data (sequences of x, y, time) for 50M drawings. Goal: Predict the object drawn. Challenge: Drawings are often abstract, messy, or incomplete; models must process both the final image and the drawing process.
solution_summary: Hybrid 1D-CNN and 2D-CNN ensemble. 1st place used a '2D CNN' (MobileNet/ResNet) on the rendered doodle image and a '1D CNN' on the raw stroke sequence. The 1D CNN captured the temporal order of drawing. They used 'Progressive Image Resizing' to speed up training and a large ensemble of models to handle the variety of drawing styles.

title: Human Protein Atlas Image Classification
prompt: Classify the subcellular localization of proteins in microscopy images. Data: 4-channel images (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow) representing different cell structures. Goal: Predict which of 28 organelles the protein is located in (multi-label). Challenge: High class imbalance and identifying patterns in 4-channel multi-spectral data.
solution_summary: Multi-head CNN with 4-channel input. 1st place used an ensemble of ResNet-50 and GapNet-styled models modified to accept 4 input channels. They utilized 'Focal Loss' to address class imbalance and applied 'External Data' from the official Human Protein Atlas website to triple the size of the minority classes. Post-processing included threshold optimization per class.

title: Recruit Restaurant Visitor Forecasting
prompt: Predict the future number of restaurant visitors in Japan. Data: Reservation data, historical visits, and holiday information. Goal: Forecast daily visitors for the next 45 days. Challenge: Capturing the interplay between reservations (which are leading indicators) and walk-in visitors.
solution_summary: Ensemble of Gradient Boosting and Neural Networks. 1st place created 'Lagged Reservation' features and 'Weighted Moving Averages' of historical visits based on the day of the week. They used a combination of XGBoost, LightGBM, and an MLP. They specifically modeled 'Golden Week' (Japanese holiday) differently due to its unique impact on foot traffic.

title: Zillow Prize: Zillow’s Home Value Prediction
prompt: Improve the 'Zestimate' accuracy by predicting the log-error of the home value model. Data: Property features (size, location, age) and transaction history. Goal: Predict the error between the actual price and Zillow's estimate. Challenge: The error is small and noisy; the model must find tiny signals in home features that the base model missed.
solution_summary: Stacking of shallow and deep models. 1st place used a stacked ensemble of XGBoost, LightGBM, and a Neural Network. They focused on 'Location-based' feature engineering, calculating the distance to nearby amenities and the 'relative' value compared to neighbors. A key technique was 'Outlier clipping'—removing extreme log-errors from training to focus the model on the typical error range.
key_techniques: Mean target encoding for Zip codes

title: PetFinder.my - Pawpularity Score Prediction
prompt: Predict the 'Pawpularity' (click rate) of shelter pet photos. Data: Pet images and categorical metadata (e.g., 'eyes', 'blur'). Goal: Predict a score from 1 to 100. Challenge: The 'Pawpularity' score is highly subjective and depends on both aesthetic and emotional qualities of the photo.
solution_summary: Fusion of Swin Transformer and Metadata. 1st place used a Swin-Large Transformer pre-trained on ImageNet-22k. They concatenated the image features with the tabular metadata at the final layer. They used a 'Binary Cross-Entropy' loss by scaling the 1-100 score to 0-1, which performed better than MSE due to the score distribution's peaks at the boundaries.
